name: Cardinal Pipeline
researcher_notes: Intrastate North Carolina gas line, in service since 1999, with no row in the roster. It is not Carolina Gas Transmission (P3221, P4381) and not the Mountain Valley Southgate row. A Cardinal Pipeline Company press release from March 2010 says the line is 105 miles and 24 inches, runs from Rockingham County to a point southeast of Raleigh, and has a design capacity of about 279,000 dekatherms per day. Its members are subsidiaries of Williams Partners, PSNC Energy and Piedmont, and it takes gas from an interconnect with Transco. The EIA pipeline projects table for August 2026 (sheet Historical Projects, Excel row 128, project name Cardinal Pipeline, operator Transcontinental Gas Pipeline) lists a completed new pipeline, 67 miles, 24 inches, 263 MMcf/d, cost 98.3 million dollars, in service November 1999, intrastate, state authority. Length conflict: 67 miles in EIA versus 105 miles from the operator. The staged value is 105 miles because the operator states it directly and it is the later figure, which likely includes later extensions. The 67 mile figure is the original 1999 build. Either is far above the 25 km threshold. The two sources are not fully independent on length because they disagree. Capacity unit is Dekatherms per day as the source states. A 2012 expansion of 199,000 Dth/d was planned in the same release and is not staged. Owner is the operating company. Member shares are not stated, so Parent is left blank. Capacity listed by EIA is 263 MMcf/d. No route found yet. Route research is still owed: check the North Carolina Utilities Commission and the state pipeline safety records. Intrastate lines do not appear in FERC filings, so silence there is not a concern. The NGI and Pipeline and Gas Journal pages from the candidate list were not used as refs: the NGI page returned 403 and the Pipeline and Gas Journal article is behind a paywall.
